title: Talking about success and failure
about: Collocations for talking about success and failure: make a breakthrough, a remarkable achievement, take advantage of, bring out the best in sb, fail miserably, hopes are dashed, a recipe for disaster, lose your nerve.

items.pattern: make a breakthrough (in / with sth) · a big / real / major breakthrough · also: achieve / have a breakthrough
items.meaning: suddenly make important progress after a long time of trying
items.uk: зробити прорив, нарешті зрушити з мертвої точки
items.example: After months of struggling with the piano, Olga finally **made a breakthrough** and played the whole piece without stopping.
more: We **made a real breakthrough** with our son's reading this term: now he reads to us every night.
For months the puppy was afraid of the car, but this week we **made a breakthrough**: he jumped in by himself.
items.watchOut: «Зробити прорив» — make a breakthrough, а не do a breakthrough. Прорив у чомусь — a breakthrough in / with sth: a breakthrough in maths, with the puppy.

items.pattern: a remarkable achievement · it's a remarkable achievement (for sb) to do sth · also: a real / great achievement
items.meaning: something impressive that someone has done, especially when it was difficult
items.example: Running a marathon at seventy-five is a **remarkable achievement**.
more: Raising four kids alone and finishing a degree at the same time was a **remarkable achievement**.
For a small village school, sending three pupils to the national finals is a **remarkable achievement**.
items.watchOut: Achievement — злічуваний іменник, тому з артиклем: That's a remarkable achievement, а не That's remarkable achievement. Remarkable — «неабиякий, вражаючий», а не просто «помітний» (noticeable).

items.pattern: a dramatic improvement (in sth) · improve dramatically · also: a big / huge / marked improvement
items.meaning: a big, quick change for the better
items.example: Since Gran started walking every day, there's been a **dramatic improvement** in her health.
more: The new owners have made a **dramatic improvement** to the café: it's busy every morning now.
After he got glasses, there was a **dramatic improvement** in Leo's handwriting.
items.watchOut: Dramatic тут — «різкий, разючий», а не «драматичний, трагічний». Поліпшення чого — зазвичай an improvement in sth: an improvement in her health, in his English.

items.pattern: sb's crowning achievement · the crowning achievement of sb's career / life
items.meaning: the best and most important thing someone has done, after many other successes
items.example: Mum has baked hundreds of cakes, but her **crowning achievement** was my sister's three-tier wedding cake.
more: Grandad made a lot of furniture, but the oak dining table was his **crowning achievement**.
Winning the regional cup was the **crowning achievement** of the coach's twenty years at the club.
items.watchOut: «Вінець (вершина) досягнень» — crowning achievement, з -ing: не crown achievement. Зазвичай з his / her / their або the … of sth: the crowning achievement of her career.

items.phrase: have a good / excellent grasp of sth
items.pattern: have a good / excellent / firm grasp of sth · a basic / poor grasp of sth
items.meaning: understand a subject or a language well
items.uk: добре розумітися на чомусь, добре знати (мову, предмет)
items.example: Dina **has an excellent grasp of** Spanish, so she did all the talking on our trip to Valencia.
more: You need **a good grasp of** basic maths to plan a family budget.
My son **has a good grasp of** the rules of chess now, but he still loses to his grandad.
items.watchOut: Grasp тут — «розуміння», а не «хватка». Після grasp зазвичай of: a good grasp of French. Близькі за змістом: a good knowledge of French, a good command of French.

items.pattern: sth comes in useful / handy (for sth / for doing sth) · will / might come in useful
items.meaning: be useful later, at a moment when you need it
items.example: Keep those cardboard boxes. They'll **come in useful** when we move.
more: My first-aid course **came in handy** when a little boy fell over in the park.
Take an umbrella. It might **come in useful** if the weather changes.
items.watchOut: «Знадобиться» — it'll come in useful / handy: тут потрібні і come, і in. Не it'll come useful. Можна й просто: it'll be useful.

items.pattern: take (full) advantage of sth (an offer, a chance, the good weather) · take advantage of sb = use sb unfairly
items.meaning: use a good situation or chance to get something good from it
items.example: We **took advantage of** the sunny weekend and painted the fence.
more: **Take advantage of** the sale: winter coats are half price this week.
Our neighbour is very kind, and some people **take advantage of** her.
items.watchOut: «Скористатися» — take advantage of, а не use the advantage чи get advantage of. Обережно з людиною: take advantage of sb — використати когось, зловживати чиєюсь добротою.

items.pattern: pass an exam / a test / your driving test · pass with good marks / with distinction
items.meaning: be successful in an exam or a test
items.example: My cousin **passed her driving test** at the first attempt.
more: If you want to **pass the exam**, start revising now, not the night before.
Ten years after leaving school, Mum **passed her English exam** with top marks.
items.watchOut: Pass an exam — успішно скласти. «Здавати іспит» (бути на іспиті, результат ще невідомий) — take / sit an exam. Тож «Завтра я здаю іспит» — I'm taking an exam tomorrow, а не I'm passing an exam.

items.pattern: success is guaranteed · guaranteed success · be guaranteed to succeed / to work
items.meaning: it will certainly be successful
items.example: With Dad's barbecue and this sunshine, the party's **success is guaranteed**.
more: If you follow Gran's recipe exactly, **success is guaranteed**.
No diet comes with **guaranteed success**, whatever the advert says.
items.watchOut: Вимова guaranteed: /ˌɡærənˈtiːd/ — u не читається, наголос на останньому складі.

items.pattern: make good / great / slow progress (with / in sth) · progress is uncountable
items.meaning: improve or move forward well
items.example: Our daughter is **making good progress** with her swimming: she can do a whole length now.
more: We **made good progress** on the motorway and reached the coast by lunchtime.
The builders are **making slow progress** because of all the rain.
items.watchOut: Progress — незлічуваний іменник: make good progress, а не a good progress і не progresses. Дієслово — make, не do.

items.pattern: gain / get good / high marks (in / for sth) · get full marks · US: grades
items.meaning: get good results in a test or a piece of school work
items.example: Maya **gained good marks** in all her science tests this term.
more: You'll **get good marks** if you show how you worked out the answer.
My little brother **got full marks** in his spelling test and wants a reward.
items.watchOut: Бал за тест чи письмову роботу британською — a mark (get full marks), підсумкова оцінка за іспит — a grade (a grade B); в американській шкільна оцінка — a grade. Але не an estimation. «Отримати хорошу оцінку» — get / gain a good mark, а не take чи make a good mark.

items.pattern: be a great / brilliant / huge success · be a success with sb
items.meaning: something that goes very well and that people like
items.example: The school's summer fair was a **great success**: we raised enough money for a new climbing frame.
more: Your lemon tart was a **brilliant success**. Everyone asked for the recipe.
The surprise party was a **huge success**, and Dad didn't suspect a thing.
items.watchOut: «Вечірка мала великий успіх» англійською зазвичай The party was a great success — з дієсловом be і артиклем a, а не The party had a big success.

items.pattern: highly effective (against / for sth) · also: highly successful / recommended / skilled
items.meaning: working very well and giving the result you want
items.example: Hot tea with honey and lemon is **highly effective** for a sore throat.
more: The new speed bumps outside the school have been **highly effective**: drivers really slow down now.
My daughter's teacher uses a **highly effective** reward chart.
items.watchOut: «Високоефективний» — highly effective, з highly, а не high effective. Highly — «дуже, надзвичайно», а high — «високий» (про висоту, рівень).

items.pattern: make a useful / valuable / big contribution (to sth) · make useful contributions in class / to a discussion
items.meaning: do or say something that helps a group, a discussion or a project
items.example: Even the youngest children **made a useful contribution** to cleaning up the beach.
more: At the residents' meeting, Mr Patel **made some useful contributions** about parking.
Everyone **made a contribution** to the wedding: my aunt did the flowers and my uncle drove us.
items.watchOut: «Робити внесок» — make a contribution, а не do a contribution. Внесок у щось — a contribution to sth: a contribution to the project.

items.phrase: have the ability to do sth
items.pattern: have the ability to do sth · have a natural / rare ability to do sth
items.meaning: be able to do something; have the skill for it
items.example: My aunt **has the ability to** calm any crying baby in a minute.
more: Not everyone **has the ability to** explain things simply.
Our dog seems to **have the ability to** hear a cheese wrapper from three rooms away.
items.watchOut: Дію після ability ставимо з to: the ability to explain, а не the ability of explaining. Of — лише перед тим, хто має здатність: the ability of children to learn.

items.phrase: an effective way of doing sth
items.pattern: an effective way of doing sth / to do sth · find effective ways of / to …
items.meaning: a method that works well and gives a good result
items.example: Walking to work is an **effective way of** staying fit without paying for a gym.
more: We need to find **effective ways to** stop the kids arguing in the car.
A bowl of vinegar is an **effective way of** getting rid of bad smells in the kitchen.
items.watchOut: Effective — дає потрібний результат; efficient — працює без зайвих витрат часу, сил чи грошей. Українське «ефективний» буває і тим, і тим. Після way — of doing або to do: a way of saving / a way to save.

items.phrase: enjoy the fruits of your hard work
items.pattern: enjoy / reap the fruits of your (hard) work / labour
items.meaning: enjoy the good results you have because you worked hard
items.example: After twenty years of saving, my parents are **enjoying the fruits of their hard work** in a little house by the sea.
more: We planted strawberries in April, and now we're **enjoying the fruits of our hard work**, quite literally!
She trained every morning for a year, and now she's **reaping the fruits of her hard work**.

items.phrase: bring out the best in sb
items.pattern: bring out the best in sb · opposite: bring out the worst in sb
items.meaning: make someone show their best qualities
items.example: Looking after her baby brother **brings out the best in** Sofia: she's so patient with him.
more: A good teacher **brings out the best in** every child, not only the clever ones.
Long car journeys **bring out the worst in** my husband.
items.watchOut: Bring out, а не bring off (bring off — успішно провернути щось складне). І in sb: brings out the best in him, а не of him чи from him.

items.pattern: win / earn / gain the respect of sb · win sb's respect
items.meaning: make people respect you because of what you do
items.example: The new nurse quickly **won the respect of** the older patients.
more: Our coach **earned the players' respect** by never missing a training session.
You don't **win people's respect** by shouting at them.
items.watchOut: «Завоювати повагу» — win / earn sb's respect, а не conquer respect: conquer — завойовувати країни, вершини, власний страх.

items.pattern: fail miserably (at sth / to do sth) · also: fail dismally / completely
items.meaning: be completely unsuccessful, often in a way that makes you feel bad
items.uk: з тріском провалитися, зазнати цілковитої невдачі
items.example: I tried to make sushi for my friends and **failed miserably**: the rice went everywhere.
more: My plan to give up chocolate **failed miserably** after two days.
We tried to keep the party a secret, but **failed miserably** when my little sister told Mum.
items.watchOut: «З тріском провалитися» — fail miserably, а не fail sadly: sadly — «на жаль, сумно». Miserably тут означає «жалюгідно, цілковито».

items.pattern: be / prove (to be) a spectacular failure · fail spectacularly
items.meaning: an extremely bad failure that everyone notices
items.example: The new shopping centre was a **spectacular failure**: half the shops closed in the first year.
more: My first soufflé was a **spectacular failure**: it collapsed in front of all the guests.
The outdoor ice rink proved to be a **spectacular failure** in such a warm winter.
items.watchOut: «Гучний провал» — a spectacular failure, а не a loud failure. Spectacular — «видовищний, приголомшливий», тому буває і a spectacular success.

items.pattern: be / prove (to be) a dismal failure · fail dismally
items.meaning: a complete failure that is depressing and disappointing
items.example: The diet was a **dismal failure**: I put on two kilos in a month.
more: Our attempt to grow tomatoes on the balcony was a **dismal failure**.
Hopes were high for the new bus service, but it's been a **dismal failure**: the buses are always late.
items.watchOut: Іменник — failure: a dismal failure, а не a dismal fail (fail як іменник — сленг: an epic fail). «Повний провал» — a complete / total / dismal failure, а не a full failure.

items.pattern: a film / play / book / product flops · be a (complete / total) flop · informal
items.meaning: fail because not enough people come to see it or buy it
items.uk: провалитися, не мати успіху (про фільм, виставу, товар)
items.example: The band's second album **flopped**, and they split up a year later.
more: The new flavour of crisps was a **complete flop**: nobody bought it.
The school play **flopped** because it was on the same night as the football final.
items.watchOut: Flop — розмовне слово, зазвичай про фільм, виставу, книгу чи товар. Буває дієсловом (the film flopped) та іменником (the film was a flop).

items.pattern: sb's hopes (of sth) are dashed · dash sb's hopes · also: hopes are shattered
items.meaning: something you hoped for becomes impossible, so you have to give up the hope
items.example: Our **hopes** of a beach holiday **were dashed** when the airline cancelled our flight.
more: Tom's **hopes** of playing in the final **were dashed** when he broke his wrist.
The rain **dashed** our **hopes** of a barbecue.
items.watchOut: «Надії розбилися» — hopes were dashed (або shattered), а не smashed: smash — розбити вщент річ (smash a window).

items.pattern: fail an exam / a test / your driving test · fail maths / history
items.meaning: not pass an exam or a test
items.example: My brother **failed his driving test** twice before he passed.
more: If you **fail the exam** in June, you can take it again in August.
She was so nervous that she **failed** the oral **exam**, though she knew all the answers.
items.watchOut: «Провалити іспит» — fail an exam, зазвичай без прийменника. Не плутай: fail an exam — не скласти; take / sit an exam — здавати (бути на іспиті).

items.pattern: sth goes badly / terribly wrong · sth goes wrong with sth
items.meaning: happen in a very bad way, with bad results
items.example: Our camping trip **went badly wrong** when the tent blew away in the night.
more: Dad's attempt to cut my hair **went badly wrong**, so I wore a hat for a week.
Something **went badly wrong** with the heating, and the whole flat was freezing.
items.watchOut: Badly, а не bad: things went badly wrong. Не плутай із go bad — зіпсуватися (про їжу): the milk has gone bad.

items.pattern: be doomed to failure · be doomed to fail · be doomed from the start
items.meaning: be certain to fail
items.example: A diet with no bread, no pasta and no sugar was **doomed to failure** in our house.
more: Their plan to sell ice cream on the beach in November was **doomed to failure**.
Without the parents' help, the school garden project was **doomed to failure**.
items.watchOut: «Приречений на провал» — doomed to failure (to + іменник) або doomed to fail (to + дієслово), без on чи at.

items.pattern: go out of business · put sb out of business
items.meaning: stop trading because the company has no money
items.example: The little bookshop on our street **went out of business** after the big store opened.
more: Several cafés in the town centre **went out of business** during the long roadworks.
The new supermarket might **put** the local butcher **out of business**.
items.watchOut: Go out of business, а не go out from business. Близькі вирази: go bankrupt (збанкрутувати), close down (закритися з будь-якої причини).

items.pattern: be a recipe for disaster / trouble
items.meaning: something that will very probably lead to big problems
items.example: Two toddlers, a white sofa and a bowl of spaghetti: that's a **recipe for disaster**.
more: Driving to the airport in rush hour with no time to spare is a **recipe for disaster**.
Going hiking in the mountains without a map is a **recipe for disaster**.
items.watchOut: Recipe /ˈresəpi/ — рецепт страви, три склади. Не плутай із receipt /rɪˈsiːt/ — чек у магазині, і з prescription — рецепт від лікаря.

items.pattern: lose your nerve · opposite: keep your nerve
items.meaning: suddenly become too frightened to do something you planned to do
items.uk: злякатися в останню мить, не наважитися
items.example: I was going to ask for a pay rise, but I **lost my nerve** at the door of my boss's office.
more: My son climbed to the top of the diving board and then **lost his nerve**.
She wanted to sing at her sister's wedding, but she **lost her nerve** and just made a toast.
items.watchOut: Nerve тут в однині: lose your nerve, а не lose your nerves. Lose your courage кажуть рідше. Множина — в іншому виразі: get on sb's nerves (дратувати).

items.pattern: miss the point (of sth) · completely / totally miss the point
items.meaning: not understand the most important part of what someone says or does
items.uk: не вловити суті, не зрозуміти головного
items.example: You've **missed the point**. I'm not angry about the money, I'm angry that you lied.
more: The film is funny, but people who think it's just a comedy **miss the point**.
My aunt totally **missed the point** of the joke and asked us to explain it.
items.watchOut: «Не зрозуміти суті» — miss the point, а не pass the point чи lose the point. Point тут — суть, головне.

warmup.uk: Вона склала всі іспити, хоча майже не готувалася.
warmup.q: She ___ all her exams, though she hardly revised.
warmup.explain: Скласти іспит (успішно) — pass an exam. «Здавати» (бути на іспиті) — take / sit an exam.

warmup.uk: Моя мама робить великі успіхи в італійській.
warmup.q: My mum is ___ great progress with her Italian.
warmup.explain: Робити успіхи — make progress. Progress — незлічуване, без a.

warmup.uk: Ми скористалися знижкою й купили новий холодильник.
warmup.q: We ___ advantage of the discount and bought a new fridge.

warmup.uk: Вона завоювала повагу учнів у перший же тиждень.
warmup.q: She ___ the respect of her pupils in her very first week.
warmup.explain: Завоювати повагу — win (або earn) the respect of sb. Conquer — завойовувати країни чи вершини.

warmup.uk: Я хотів стрибнути з парашутом, але в останню мить злякався.
warmup.q: I wanted to do a parachute jump, but I ___ at the last moment.
warmup.explain: Lose your nerve — злякатися, не наважитися. Nerve тут в однині.

warmup.uk: Наші надії на перемогу розбилися в останню хвилину матчу.
warmup.q: Our hopes of winning were ___ in the last minute of the match.
warmup.explain: Надії розбилися — hopes were dashed (або shattered). Smash — розбити вщент річ.

warmup.uk: Вони не зрозуміли суті моєї пропозиції.
warmup.q: They ___ the point of my suggestion.
warmup.explain: Не зрозуміти суті — miss the point.

warmup.uk: Заводити собаку, коли ти цілий день на роботі, — прямий шлях до біди.
warmup.q: Getting a dog when you're at work all day is a ___ for disaster.
warmup.explain: A recipe for disaster — прямий шлях до біди. Recipe — рецепт страви, receipt — чек, prescription — рецепт від лікаря.

A.q: After two weeks in the job, she already has a good ___ of how the shop works.
A.explain: A good grasp of sth — добре розуміння чогось.

A.q: After weeks of tears at the school gate, we finally ___ a breakthrough: Lily walked in without looking back.
Being a big brother has really brought ___ the best in Max.
A.explain: Bring out the best in sb — розкрити найкраще в людині. Bring off — успішно провернути щось складне; bring up — виховувати.

B.q: I tried to stay calm in the job interview but failed ___.
B.explain: Fail miserably — з тріском провалитися. Sadly — «на жаль».

B.q: The video rental shop on our street went out of ___ years ago.
B.explain: Go out of business — збанкрутувати, закритися (про фірму, магазин).

B.q: Trying to teach a cat to walk on a lead was ___ to failure.
B.explain: Doomed to failure — приречений на провал.

example.title: The café on Mill Street
example.uk:
Коли моя тітка відкрила кав'ярню на Млинарській вулиці, друзі казали, що це прямий шлях до біди. Дві кав'ярні поблизу щойно збанкрутували, а її перше меню провалилося.

Але вона не злякалася. Вона скористалася літнім ярмарком і продавала тістечка натовпам відвідувачів. Її лимонний пиріг мав великий успіх, і до осені вона вже робила помітні успіхи. Та в грудні її надії на жваве Різдво розбилися: прорвало трубу, і кав'ярню довелося зачинити на місяць.

Навесні вона знову відкрила кав'ярню, і цього разу все пішло добре. Минулого тижня кав'ярня отримала нагороду як найкращий малий бізнес міста. Це вершина її досягнень, і тепер вона нарешті пожинає плоди своєї важкої праці.
example.en:
When my aunt opened a café on Mill Street, her friends said it was [[a recipe for disaster|b10]]. Two cafés nearby had just [[gone out of business|b9]], and her first menu [[flopped|b4]].

But she didn't [[lose her nerve|b11]]. She [[took advantage of|a7]] the summer fair and sold cakes to the crowds. Her lemon cake was [[a great success|a12]], and by autumn she was [[making good progress|a10]]. Then, in December, her [[hopes of a busy Christmas were dashed|b5]]: a pipe burst, and the café had to close for a month.

She opened again in spring, and this time everything went well. Last week the café won the prize for the best small business in town. It's her [[crowning achievement|a4]], and she's finally [[enjoying the fruits of her hard work|a17]].
